_comment: Every external input this project depends on, with where to get it and what
it must hash to. This file is committed; the artefacts are not.
Rule: a source is not usable until its hash is recorded here. `tools/fetch-sources.sh`
refuses to report success on a file whose hash does not match, and refuses to
silently skip one it could not fetch.
base        the primary source tree the build is derived from
reference   read and cross-checked against, never built from
baseline    the upstream RE project, pinned, read-only, supplies the differential
now         needed before R0/R2 can start
later       needed at the gate named in `needed_by`
manual      cannot be scripted; a human obtains it

pin.subject: A guard case that expired on the day the thing it guards started working

upstream.why: The differential proof in R9 is only credible if the baseline it compares against is one this project cannot edit. The commit hash IS that proof.

source_trees.pin_note: The commit this project actually read, recorded 2026-08-26. A --depth 1 clone of a moving branch is not a citable artefact; a quotation from a file needs the revision it was quoted from.
source_trees.why: The only public drop whose target board IS an RTL8196E (ALFA AIP-W512). Carries linux-2.6.30, busybox-1.13, users/, romfs/, boards/rtl8196eu/, and THREE rsdk toolchains.

contains.toolchain_note: CORRECTED 2026-08-27: this entry said BOTH toolchains and listed two; the drop carries THREE, and the one it omitted is the only one whose target core is this SoC's. It is also the one that did the work in R2a/b/d-2: its `as` supplied the per-core ISA table (tools/isa-probe.sh) and its objdump did the MIPS16 disassembly. All three run natively in the WSL distro -- no container -- which refutes the premise of step R2a/b/d-3. Measured versions: 1.3.6 pair are gcc 3.4.6-1.3.6; 1.5.5 is gcc 4.4.5-1.5.5p4, against this device's banner of 4.4.5-1.5.5p2. rsdk-1.5.5's `as` does not start: it needs an i386 libz.so.1 the distro lacks, which is why -S and objdump were used instead.

source_trees.matches_device: gcc 4.4.5-1.5.5p2 / uClibc 0.9.30.3 / Linux 2.6.30.9 — every field of the device's own kernel banner. HYPOTHESIS until R2a measures it.
source_trees.caveat: ALFA's board, not TOTOLINK's. DDR timing, PHY config and GPIO pin assignment may all differ, and getting them wrong does not necessarily crash.

source_trees.why: The only public source for the rtl819x BOOTLOADER (rtl819x/bootcode/). Needed to read what the loader does, and for R10c if a first-stage loader is ever attempted. ALSO (2026-08-26): rtl819x/boards/rtl8196e/config.linux-2.6.30.* -- the vendor's own kernel config for THIS SoC, five board variants, all carrying ARCH_CACHE_WBC=y (write-back), ARCH_CPU_RLX4181=y, ARCH_CPU_ULS=y, and LLSC/SYNC not set. It is the second copy of the same Realtek SDK config as saturn49-wecb, so the two agree by descent and are ONE vote, not two.
source_trees.caveat: A different bootcode generation from this unit's 2014.04.22 v1.3. Do not assume the command set matches — the device's own `?` output (upstream notes/uart-pinout.md) is authoritative.
source_trees.needed_by: R0 (reading), R10c (writing), R1h (the write-back vote against probe1's reading)

source_trees.why: rtl819x/users/boa/apmib/apmib.{c,h} — the MIB table the device's libapmib.so is a build of. Upstream already used it to give the recovered MIB table an outside witness (SUPER_NAME=180, USER_NAME=182). ALSO (2026-08-26): rtl819x/linux-2.6.30/arch/rlx/mm/cache-rlx.c -- "RLX specific mmu/cache code", Realtek, Tony Wu, 2008-12-07. It is the ONLY source in this project that NAMES the CP0-20 (CCTL) commands (0x1 DInval, 0x2 IInval, 0x100 DWB, 0x200 DWB_Inval) and the cache-op field encoding (0x10/0x11/0x15/0x19/0x1b). Plus boards/rtl8196e/config.linux-2.6.30.* as above.
source_trees.needed_by: R2b, R7b (config store schema), D8 (CVE-2024-21778 TLV parser), R1-gate + R1h (CCTL command names; notes/cache-model.md)

source_trees.why: Realtek's own OpenWrt SDK. Carries arch/rlx (the Lexra kernel architecture port), drivers/net/rtl819x/ (rtl865x_*), drivers/net/wireless/rtl8192cd/.
source_trees.caveat: ODM-quality code. Read it as a description of what the hardware needs, never as a model of how to write a driver.

source_trees.why: A SECOND independent implementation of the rtl819x network driver (target/linux/realtek/files/drivers/net/rtl819x/, incl. rtl_nic.c). Two implementations of the same hardware is what makes a register reading a measurement instead of a transcription.
SDK v3.4.9.3 on Linux 3.10 — the K2 candidate, i.e. the first kernel generation where MIPS has device tree.
source_trees.caveat: Its documented targets are RTL8198C/8814/8194. Whether RTL8196E is supported is UNVERIFIED.

source_trees.why: The furthest anyone has publicly taken RTL8196E on a modern kernel: OpenWrt master + Linux 4.14, arch/rlx, with GPIO/PCI/IRQ/timers working. K3 reference.
source_trees.caveat: 'Working' is a forum claim, not a measurement. Switch driver incomplete, WiFi not started.

source_trees.why: The `files` branch carries the vendor datasheets. This is where refs/*.pdf come from.

A modern-kernel RTL8196E port carrying arch/mips/boot/dts/realtek/{rtl8196e.dtsi, rtl8196e_totolink_n100re.dts} -- a device tree for a TOTOLINK board on this SoC -- plus CPU_RLX4181 in cpu_type_enum, -march=rlx4181, R3000 cache paths, wait-instruction support, rdhwr emulation and a defconfig. It is the closest prior art to R5's drivers and DT bindings and to R10a/R10b.
source_trees.consumed_as: SECOND IMPLEMENTATION, NOT AN ANSWER. D12 source class 5: same SoC, so stronger than a sister-core document; written by someone who was also guessing, so weaker than a vendor SDK. One vote. Its use is to generate advance predictions and to fill the comparison column of docs/driver-diff.md -- R5 writes its drivers blind first, then diffs.
source_trees.caveat: Completeness is claimed by its author and its README, not established here. The first thing to do with it is read rtl8196e.dtsi's compatible strings and register addresses and check them against SPEC.md section 9 -- values already read on this unit. If they disagree, this tree may not be describing this part.

documents.handling: CITE, DO NOT COMMIT. See plan/router-rebuild-plan.md D12.

supplies.timer_watchdog: base 0xB800_3100 — TC0DATA 3100, TC1DATA 3104, TC0CNT 3108, TC1CNT 310C, TCCNR 3110, TCIR 3114, CDBR 3118, WDT 311C (sec 8.2)
supplies.spi_flash: controller with memory-mapped read, serial + dual I/O, up to 96.875 MHz (sec 7.3/7.4)
supplies.switch_core: base 0xBB80_4000 — Global Port Control 4000, MDC/MDIO Command 4004, MDC/MDIO Status 4008 (sec 11.1); LED control + topology + SCAN mode (sec 11.3)
supplies.pcie: host mode base 0xB8B0_1000 (sec 10.3) — NOTE: 0xB8B0 is PCIe, NOT the network MAC
supplies.pinmux: sec 6.1 Configuration upon Power-On Strapping, sec 6.2 Shared I/O Pin Mapping
supplies.ejtag: standard 5-signal P1149.1 test port (sec 1); DC params sec 13.10; boundary scan sec 14.2.4
supplies.cpu_claim: 'Embedded RISC CPU, RLX4181 with 16KB I-Cache, 8KB D-Cache, 16KB I-MEM, 8KB D-MEM' / 'Supports MIPS-1 ISA, MIPS16 ISA' / 'Clock Rate: 400MHz'
supplies.absent: no crypto / security engine section anywhere in the table of contents

caveats: It is a DRAFT. Draft and production silicon can differ.
It is the -VE1/2/3 variant, which has embedded DRAM by MCM. THIS UNIT HAS EXTERNAL SDRAM (Winbond W9825G6KH) and is therefore NOT this part.
Its CPU claim (RLX4181, MIPS-1) contradicts the common 'RTL8196E = RLX5281' convention AND the 142 lwl/lwr/swl/swr instructions in this device's own /bin/boa. See plan F34 and gate R1.
Therefore: no register value goes into code on this document's authority alone. Two independent sources, always (D12).

documents.kind_of_document: SCANNED IMAGES (11 CCITTFaxDecode streams, no text layer). Machine text extraction fails and correctly reports failure. A human reads it.
documents.why: The sibling part. Its CPU/Features bullet on the first pages is a FOURTH independent source for F34: if it also says RLX4181, the 'C=4181 / E=5281' convention is wrong in both directions and the R1 measurement is the only thing left standing.
documents.task: plan/DAY-ZERO.md item 6 — read one bullet with your eyes, ten seconds.

documents.title: Lexra LX4189 Data Sheet, Release 1.9
documents.handling: CITE, DO NOT COMMIT -- CLAUDE.md forbids committing a datasheet. Fetched 2026-08-26 (R1h-1); it lives under $FWRE_WORK and the sha256 above is what pins the copy any claim here was read out of.

supplies.cctl_bitmap: sec 5.2: bit 7 IROMOff, 6 IROMOn, 5 IMEMOff, 4 IMEMFill, 3-2 ILock, 1 IInval, 0 DInval. EDGE-TRIGGERED on 0->1. This is what names CCTL 0x010/0x020 (SPEC.md CPU-24).
supplies.status_figure: sec 3.4.1: 31-28 CU(3:0), 27-23 zero, 22 BEV, 21-16 zero, 15-8 IM(7:0), 7-6 zero, 5-0 the KU/IE stack. 'The 0 fields are ignored on write and are 0 on read.' SOURCE FOR probe3's s-isc CONTROL BITS 6 AND 24, and it also predicts bit 16 (IsC) reading back CLEAR -- on this part IsC and SwC do not exist.
supplies.cp0_register_list: Table 2: CP0 registers are 8 BADVADDR, 12 STATUS, 13 CAUSE, 14 EPC, 15 PRID, 20 CCTL -- AND NOTHING ELSE. NO TLB. This die has 32 TLB entries (CPU-08), so the LX4189 is a SIBLING AND DEMONSTRABLY NOT THIS PART.
supplies.prid: Table 2: PRID reads 0x0000c401 for the LX4189. This unit reads 0x0000CD01 (CPU-04). ONE POINT on the Lexra PRId map and the first this project has had -- it says 0xCD01 is not an LX4189 and NOTHING MORE. CLAUDE.md's ban on writing RLX4181/RLX5281 stands: this is a datum, not an assignment table.
supplies.cache_geometry: sec 5.1 Table 18: ICACHE is 'Direct mapped or two-way set associative'; DCACHE is 'Direct mapped' and Table 25 offers no other form. Line size configurable 16/32/64/128 bytes (sec 5.1) = 4/8/16/32 words (sec 5.6). Narrows probe3's associativity cells from no-source-at-all to {1,2} on the I side and direct-mapped on the D side.
supplies.coherence: sec 5.2, and it is what refuted two probe3 cells: 'perform an uncached read of the affected memory locations. If the location is resident in the data cache it will be invalidated.' and 'Note that a write to a KSEG1 address has no affect on the contents of the data cache.' Also sec 5.1: 'Caches do not snoop the system bus.' -- which is the KSEG0/KSEG1 proxy assumption R6 has to re-test with a real engine.
supplies.write_buffer: sec 5.6: 'Writes that are serviced by the data cache may require extra time to be serviced by the LBC if its write buffer is full.' Sources probe3's c-E0 write-buffer control.
supplies.exception_vector: sec 3.4.2: RESET 0xbfc0_0000; other exceptions with BEV=0 go to 0x8000_0080. A FOURTH independent source for the vector, from the core vendor.
supplies.exccodes: sec 3.4: Bp = 9, RI = 10, CpU = 11 -- the two probe3 exercises under qemu.

caveats: LX4189 IS NOT THIS CORE. It is write-through with no DWB/DWBInval, so its CCTL bits 8-9 are Reserved where this SoC's are live; and Table 2 gives it no TLB at all while this die has 32 entries (CPU-08, and Random reading 5..29 on probe2's census). Every claim taken from it is READ ABOUT A RELATED PART.

Sources CONTRADICT on CCTL bits 6-7: LX4189 IROMOn/IROMOff vs rlxregs.h's IMEM0ON at bit 6 and nothing at bit 7, vs hackpascal's ILock = 0xc0 colliding with its own IROM0ON/IROM0OFF. 0x040/0x080 stay undetermined -- SPEC.md CPU-24 residual.

IMEM/DMEM BASE and TOP are HARDWIRED CFG_ pins on the LX4189 (sec 5.4, CFG_IWBASE[31:10] / CFG_IWTOP[17:10]), not CP3 registers. This SoC's core exposes them to software -- its kernel writes CP3 $0/$1/$4/$5 -- so the CP3 numbering has ONE source (third-party lxregs.h) plus this unit's own behaviour, and the core vendor's document does NOT corroborate it.
used_by: SPEC.md CPU-04, CPU-19, CPU-24, CPU-25, CPU-45, CPU-46

documents.title: MIPS IV Instruction Set, Revision 3.2
documents.revision: Rev 3.2, September 1995, Charles Price, MIPS Technologies Inc.
documents.handling: CITE, DO NOT COMMIT -- CLAUDE.md's rule is about someone else's property, and this is. Fetched 2026-08-27 (R1h-1); it lives under $FWRE_WORK and the sha256 above pins the copy every claim here was read out of.
documents.why: It settles which ISA level owns primary opcode 0x13, which tools/hazlint and tools/opcount.py both had wrong, and -- more importantly -- it is the source for the sentence that stopped the fix from going too far.

supplies.cop3_lifetime: A 8.3.4, p. A-176, verbatim: "Coprocessor 3 is optional and implementation-specific in the MIPS I and MIPS II architecture levels. It was removed from MIPS III and later architecture levels. Note that in MIPS IV the COP3 primary opcode was reused for the COP1X instruction class." TWO claims and BOTH are load-bearing: (a) 0x13 is COP3 here, not COP1X -- this core is MIPS-I, Config.M = 0 measured; (b) OPTIONAL, so being MIPS-I is not evidence the silicon executes it, which is why hazlint --isa still reports probe3's eight mfc3 and why cell m-imem exists. SPEC.md TC-08.
supplies.encoding_tables: Table A-37 (MIPS I) and the MIPS II table both show COP3 at opcode row 2 col 3 = 0x13; the MIPS III table shows `*` annotated `(was COP3)`, with `(was LWC3)` at 0x33 and `(was SWC3)` at 0x3B; the MIPS IV table shows COP1X. The four tables are the same statement drawn four times.
supplies.second_source: binutils 2.42, measured on this machine 2026-08-27 and re-run by tools/test-hazlint.sh E3: mips-linux-gnu-as accepts `mfc3 $2,$0` at -march=mips1 and mips2 (0x4c020000), refuses it at mips3 and mips4, and accepts `lwxc1` only from mips4 (0x4ca40000). Two sources, one read and one measured, agreeing.

documents.caveat: The paragraph quoted above ends by repeating the last TWO sentences of A 8.3.3 verbatim -- "No standard processor from MIPS has implemented coprocessor 2, but MIPS' semiconductor licensees may have implemented it in a product based on one of the standard MIPS processors. At this time the standard processors are: R2000, R3000, ..." -- inside the section about coprocessor THREE. A copy-paste defect in the document, noted here so a later reader does not think this project mis-transcribed it, and corrected on 2026-08-27 from "the last sentence" after a reader checked it against the PDF. It does not touch the three sentences above.
documents.also_at: A 98,471-byte re-rendered extract of Appendix A alone (sha256 99128c1a02e3f0ab69fe76f3245bd252069e7af9f8fa1d3e6ae034118813d34d) circulates as mips-iv-encodings.pdf; it was read first and the full document above was fetched to check it. Same wording.
documents.not_in_fetch_plan: No `fetch` key, matching ds-lexra-lx4189: tools/fetch-sources.sh only plans entries whose dest is inside the repo, and this one lives under $FWRE_WORK because CLAUDE.md forbids committing it. So nothing re-checks the sha256 automatically -- it is pinned by this entry and by whoever reads the file next, which is stated rather than implied.

platform.about: ggbruno's RTL8196E/97D/97F port to OpenWrt master + Linux 4.14. What works, what does not.
The long Realtek SoC support thread. Contains the EJTAG/Lexra notes: tjtag v3.0.1 and UrJTAG needed device IDs added; eJTAG pins muxed with EPHY_LED on some parts.
RFC: rtl8196 status — historical statement that mainline has no lexra support.
RFC v2: MIPS Lexra LX5280 CPU + Realtek RTL8186 SoC support. The mainline attempt.
Lexra history — cores execute virtually all MIPS instructions EXCEPT unaligned loads and stores. The patent story behind F34.
CONFIG_OF_FLATTREE landed in 2.6.34; MIPS device tree in 2.6.37. Source for F20.
Published spec: RTL8196C + 2 MB flash + 16 MB RAM. WRONG for this unit on all three counts — which is why a second-hand spare may genuinely be a different board.

binutils-2.24 Lexra patch. Adds six cores (lx4180, rlx4181, rlx4281, rlx5181, lx5280, rlx5281), all ISA_MIPS1; instruction masks INSN_4180=0x20000000 .. INSN_5281=0x00000040 and the RLXA/RLXB/RAD1/RAD2 groupings; 100+ Lexra-proprietary mnemonics (mta2/mfa/diva/multa/madda/msuba, lt/ltp/lwp/lhp/lbp/stp/swp, addr/subr/min/max/absr/cls/mux2, cmveqz/cmvnez, mtru/mfru/mtrk/mfrk, mflxc0/mtlxc0). Source of R1a's named Lexra ASE row (F52). NOTE: it does NOT disable lwl/lwr/swl/swr -- the assembler still accepts them. WHEN THIS IS FIRST DOWNLOADED (R2c) IT MOVES TO documents WITH A sha256.

gcc-4.8.4 Lexra patch. Maps TUNE_RLX onto TUNE_MIPS3000 (R3000 scheduling); disables lwl/lwr/swl/swr generation for Lexra targets via !TARGET_LEXRA && !TARGET_RLX on those patterns; adds -mno-bdsl (flag_fix_bdsl) forbidding loads in BRANCH delay slots -- which is NOT the load-use delay of F46, a distinction the plan must keep; gates conditional move on INSN_RLXB, which is what lets CPU-17's 18 movz/movn rule out baseline LX4180. Supplies -march=rlx5281 for D1's toolchain T-B. WHEN THIS IS FIRST DOWNLOADED (R2c) IT MOVES TO documents WITH A sha256.
Second RTL8196E Linux port; see source_trees/shibajee-linux-rtl8196e. Listed here too because it is cited in the plan before it is cloned.

A PUBLIC, redistributable RTL8196E-CG datasheet mirrored by a distributor -- not the leaked -VEx draft in refs/. Names the core RLX4181. Its value is that it can be linked from a public README where the leaked draft cannot, and that it is a second document (not the same one) on the naming question. It does not settle CPU-04: the device still says neither, and only PRId does.
